prompt: Many credit 476 A.D. as the end of the Western Roman Empire when Odoacer deposed Romulus Augustus, however, one can argue this would only be based on the end of imperial legitimacy. But when can one say was the year that the Western Roman Empire was beyond saving and doomed to fall even before 476 A.D.? Would it be when the Vandals invaded Rome in 455 A.D. or sometime before or after that?
judge_reasoning: Candidate 1 most directly addresses the prompt by arguing for a “beyond saving” timeframe in the mid-5th century, tying it to specific pivotal losses (especially North Africa) even before 476. Candidate 2 provides relevant decline factors but never selects or defends a concrete “year beyond saving” in the requested way. Candidate 3 lists several 5th-century invasions and impacts but similarly avoids committing to a specific “doomed” year. Candidate 4 largely reframes the discussion around Odoacer and 476 and contains multiple clear historical inaccuracies (e.g., claiming Odoacer founded the Ostrogothic kingdom and miscasting the control/political sequence), making it the weakest.
